summary: The supporting-line and finite-tilt argument correctly forces at least W/4 mass on each closed lattice ray through z_0. For every halfspace through the anchor centroid, the proof then correctly handles degenerate restrictions and, in the ordinary case, combines fiberwise Brunn--Minkowski log-concavity, Grünbaum's centroid inequality, the accepted one-sided log-concave threshold bound, and the ray mass estimate to obtain the uniform lower bound q_d W/4 > W/64. Boundary reduction and upper semicontinuity give the stated depth bound and fiberwise maximizer conclusion. All hypotheses, zero-volume sections, boundary mass, and strict-constant steps are accounted for.
